newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - Leading light copper to shine on.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - Leading light copper to shine on.

text.p: Base metal business will be slow to develop this week, with markets closed in the U.K. and the U.S., although a strong copper market is expected to unfold once more, traders and analysts said.
On Monday, the London Metal Exchange (LME) in the U.K. is closed for the late Spring Bank Holiday, while the U.S. futures market is shut for Memorial Day.
"It will be a bit slow to start with, but it looks in good shape. People squared up before the weekend, but copper is not far off the (one-year) highs," one trader said.
Copper peaked at $2,530 a tonne last week, and although there was a late Friday upward foray, there was enough profit-taking around to keep a lid on prices.
Stocks are falling consistently, and on an overall basis approaching historically critically low levels.
Fundamentals remain strong, with demand good in most regions and new-mined supply not available until later in the year.
"We know that demand is good, but that is not the issue. It is supply, and don't forget the Kennecott smelter could re-open soon," one analyst said.
This could amount to a significant sea-change this week, if the smelter at Garfield re-opens after a maintainance shut-down that started in mid-April.
In 1996, this smelter produced just 56,000 tonnes of refined copper, against a name-plate capacity of 280,000 tonnes.
If the re-start is smooth and the plant gets up to optimum efficiency then excess stocks of ore will be smelted into deliverable refined metal.
Aluminium inventories are falling as well, but the market is is not making significant headway, despite copper strength.
Last week, inventories dropped 16,200 tonnes. The year has seen 172,925 tonnes removed from the LME.
"The concern about the stocks is that they are coming off, but they are not going into consumption - they are just being stored elsewhere," William Adams of LME trader Rudolf Wolff and Co said.
Nevertheless, aluminium is active, with investment fund interest being sucked into the market, so targets around $1,650 and the 1997 high of $1,701 cannot be ruled out, traders said.
